question: What percentage profit is made when the selling price of 12 pens covers the cost price of 27 pens?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ SP of 12 pens = CP of 27 pens

⇒ Ratio SP : CP = 27 : 12

⇒ Profit% = (27 − 12)/12 × 100

⇒ = 15/12 × 100 = 125%

**∴ Answer = 125%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of 12 pens = Cost price of 27 pens

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP of 1 pen = 1

⇒ CP of 27 pens = 27

⇒ SP of 12 pens = 27

⇒ SP of 1 pen = 27 ÷ 12

⇒ Profit per pen = (27/12 − 1)

⇒ = (27 − 12)/12 = 15/12

⇒ Profit % = (15/12) × 100 = 125%

**∴ Final Answer = 125%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Basic Concept:** Assume CP = 1 for simplicity

**Ratio Method:** Directly compare SP and CP quantities

**Profit Formula:** (SP − CP)/CP × 100

**Exam Tip:** Use unitary method for faster calculation
